answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to forge a verifiable stake bond before it can trade: the agent locks collateral that is slashed if the same operator is caught running duplicates. Creating a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand bonds, while a reef of honest peers cross-checks behaviour and flags copies. A fable of free identities collapses once every new face must pay real, losable collateral to join.
